# Geometry and Surface Priors

Also called: Geometric constraints, Surface alignment, Depth priors

## Overview
This family of methods addresses the fundamental limitation of vanilla 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS): the production of "floating" volumetric ellipsoids that lack an explicit, watertight geometric boundary [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md). By aligning the discrete Gaussian representation with continuous geometric priors (such as SDFs, depth maps, or explicit meshes), these methods enforce positional and normal consistency to enable accurate mesh extraction, physically-based rendering, and robust initialization [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md). Unlike sibling methods that may rely solely on photometric loss or implicit constraints, this family explicitly integrates geometric supervision into the training or post-processing pipeline to ensure the Gaussians conform to physical surfaces [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md).

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the goal of aligning the discrete Gaussian representation with a continuous geometric prior [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md). The core mechanism involves adding geometric loss terms to the standard photometric rendering loss $\mathcal{L}_{rgb}$ [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md). These losses typically enforce two properties:
1.  **Positional Consistency:** Gaussian centers $\mathbf{c}_i$ are encouraged to lie on the zero-level set of a distance function (SDF or UDF) or align with metric depth estimates [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md).
2.  **Normal Consistency:** The orientation of the Gaussians (derived from their covariance matrix or rotation quaternion) is aligned with the surface normal estimated from the geometric prior [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md).

The total loss function generally takes the form:
$$ \mathcal{L}_{total} = \mathcal{L}_{rgb} + \lambda_{geo} \mathcal{L}_{geo} + \lambda_{norm} \mathcal{L}_{norm} $$
where $\mathcal{L}_{geo}$ is the geometric consistency loss and $\mathcal{L}_{norm}$ is the normal consistency loss [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md). The weights $\lambda_{geo}$ and $\lambda_{norm}$ are hyperparameters that balance photometric fidelity against geometric accuracy [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md).

## Subtopics

### NeuSG
NeuSG [9172-neusg] integrates the NeuS implicit surface reconstruction method into the 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representation to transfer explicit surface properties to the discrete Gaussian primitives [9172-neusg]. It solves the problem of vanilla 3DGS producing "floating ellipsoids" rather than coherent surfaces by enforcing geometric consistency [9172-neusg]. Unlike siblings that use monocular depth or explicit mesh extraction, NeuSG directly couples a NeuS-style Signed Distance Function (SDF) with a Gaussian rasterizer [9172-neusg].

### [Monocular Depth Scale Alignment](9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment.md)
Monocular Depth Scale Alignment [9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment] is a post-optimization step in 3D Gaussian Splatting pipelines that resolves the up-to-scale ambiguity inherent in multi-view reconstruction by aligning the metric scale of optimized 3D Gaussians with metric-scale monocular depth estimates [9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment, S1]. Unlike methods that integrate depth priors during training, this approach operates after the standard Gaussian optimization phase, fixing the Gaussian parameters and optimizing only a global scale factor [9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment]. It is distinct from sibling methods like [NeuSG](9172-neusg.md) or [GSDF](9205-gsdf.md) which embed geometric losses into the training loop, and from [Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting with Depth Priors](9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors.md) which may rely on different initialization strategies [9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment].

### [Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting with Depth Priors](9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors.md)
This method [9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors] addresses the challenge of 3D reconstruction from sparse-view inputs, where standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) suffers from geometric ambiguity and artifacts due to insufficient multi-view constraints [9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [NeuSG](9172-neusg.md) and [GSDF](9205-gsdf.md) by explicitly integrating depth priors estimated from pre-trained 2D monocular depth estimation networks to supervise the Gaussian distribution, rather than relying solely on implicit neural fields or surface extraction techniques [9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors, S1].

### GSDF
GSDF [9205-gsdf] is a training optimization technique that aligns the discrete 3D Gaussian representation with a continuous Signed Distance Function (SDF) prior to enhance geometry reconstruction quality [9205-gsdf, S1]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [NeuSG](9172-neusg.md) by explicitly transferring surface properties from a neural SDF to the Gaussians, encouraging Gaussian centers to lie on the zero-level set and normals to align with the SDF gradient [9205-gsdf, S1].

### [GaussianPro](9167-gaussianpro.md)
GaussianPro [9167-gaussianpro] mitigates reconstruction artifacts and improves geometric fidelity by introducing a progressive propagation strategy [9167-gaussianpro, S1, S2]. It utilizes propagated depth and normal maps from neighboring views to guide the growth and adjustment of Gaussians [9167-gaussianpro]. It sets itself apart by explicitly enforcing normal consistency between neighboring views and introducing planar constraints, ensuring that the discrete Gaussian representation aligns more closely with continuous surface geometry [9167-gaussianpro, S1, S2].

### 3DGSR
3DGSR [S1] encourages consistency between Signed Distance Function (SDF) and 3DGS to enhance geometry reconstruction quality [S1].

### Gaussian Splatting Surface Refinement
Gaussian Splatting Surface Refinement [S2] uses pretrained volume rendering priors (UDF) to push Gaussians toward true surfaces by optimizing along the direction of increasing rendering weights, avoiding off-surface drift and discreteness [S2]. It is a post-training refinement strategy that uses a pretrained volume rendering prior to optimize Gaussian distributions toward true surfaces, particularly effective for open and thin structures [S2]. It integrates the prior into existing Gaussian Splatting variants (e.g., GaussianUDF, QGS) without modifying inference-time resource costs, as the prior network is bypassed during inference [S2]. It outperforms handcrafted renderers and closed-surface-tailored 3DGS methods on open and thin structures, where standard Gaussian distributions degrade severely [S2].

## Background
The problem of "floating" Gaussians in standard 3DGS has been a primary driver for geometric priors [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md). Early works like NeuSG [9172-neusg] adapted implicit surface representations (NeuS) to guide Gaussian placement [9172-neusg]. Subsequent works such as GSDF [9205-gsdf] and 3DGSR [S1] encouraged the consistency between SDFs and Gaussian attributes [S1]. More recent approaches leverage monocular depth estimators for scale alignment [9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment, S1] or sparse-view reconstruction [9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors, S1]. Volume rendering priors, such as those in VRP-UDF [S2], have been used to refine surfaces, particularly for thin structures where standard methods fail [S2].
